title: Celestial Art
caption: The young star cluster RCW 38, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Dark tendrils of dust thread through the bright core of the young star cluster RCW 38 in this view from ESO's Very Large Telescope, and clouds of brightly glowing gas surround the cluster. The VLT captured the region in fine detail.

The image was taken while testing the HAWK-I camera together with the GRAAL adaptive optics system. Adaptive optics measures how Earth's turbulent atmosphere blurs incoming light and corrects for it in real time, so a ground-based telescope can produce much sharper images than it otherwise could.

HAWK-I works in near-infrared light, which passes through dust more easily than visible light. That is an advantage in a young cluster like RCW 38, where dust threads through the region, as the dark tendrils show.

understand.summary: This is a near-infrared image from the HAWK-I camera on the VLT, working with the GRAAL adaptive optics system and using J, H and Ks filters. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
filters: 1.258 μm · Infrared J (Very Large Telescope HAWK-I)
1.62 μm · Infrared H (Very Large Telescope HAWK-I)
2.146 μm · Infrared Ks (Very Large Telescope HAWK-I)
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and adaptive optics undoes much of the blurring caused by Earth's atmosphere.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: RCW 38 lies in the direction of the constellation Vela. The image combines three near-infrared filters, J, H and Ks, and covers a field about eight arcminutes across. Test observations like this check that new instruments work as designed before regular science begins.
alt: A young star cluster surrounded by brightly glowing gas, with dark tendrils of dust running through its bright core.
